facts.text: On 25 April 2024 Venice became the first city in the world to make day-trippers pay to enter, as a trial.
In the 2024 trial, day visitors paid 5 euros on 29 busy days between late April and mid-July, during daytime hours.
Day visitors register and pay online and receive a QR code; there are no turnstiles, and inspectors make random checks.
People caught without registering can be fined 50 to 300 euros.
Overnight visitors staying in the city do not pay the fee because they already pay a tax on their stay; residents, students, workers and children under 14 are also exempt.
In 2025 the fee applied on 54 days, up from 29 in 2024.
In 2025 the ticket cost 5 euros if bought at least 4 days ahead and 10 euros if bought within 3 days of the visit.
The 2025 fee days fell in April, May, June and July, and the ticket was needed only for daytime arrivals.
facts.note: France 24 只寫 2025 年的收費日分布在 4–7 月；逐日日期未查證，選文只說部落客挑了 5 月的一個收費日

facts.text: Fewer than 50,000 official residents live in Venice's historic center, about 49,000 in 2024.
About 20 million people visited Venice in 2023, roughly half of them staying overnight.
Critics, including an opposition city councillor, said the 2024 fee failed to reduce crowds, and officials admitted large crowds remained.
Critics argued the city should focus on housing for residents, who have been moving to the mainland for decades as tourism takes over homes.
Large cruise ships are banned from the Venetian lagoon.
In 2023 Venice narrowly avoided being put on UNESCO's list of World Heritage in Danger.
